findings.highlight: I've left those articles to a pro
findings.evidenceJa: そっちの記事は編プロに任せてある
findings.explanation: Hamada says the music-focused articles have been entrusted to an editorial production company. The translation reads 編プロ as an individual professional and erases the separate contractor.
findings.japanese:
「いいよ、そっちの記事は編プロに任せてある。
お前が担当するのはあくまでも、
神秘のベールに包まれた冬馬かずさの『私』の部分だ」
findings.todokanai: "That's fine. I've left those articles to a pro. Your job is purely to unveil the mysterious character behind the veil of Touma Kazusa."

findings.highlight: I don't think this'll be a meager job
findings.evidenceJa: 『こんな芸能ネタで』と思わないでもないけど
findings.explanation: Haruki cannot entirely suppress the dismissive thought 'over entertainment gossip like this.' The translation instead says he does not think the assignment will be meager, reversing his opening evaluation before the line reaches its own contrary conclusion.
findings.japanese:
『こんな芸能ネタで』と思わないでもないけど、
ま、入社一年目の新人社員に全面的に任せるんだから、
その程度の仕事ってことなんだろう…多分。
findings.todokanai: I don't think this'll be a meager job, but if it's something they're willing to completely hand over to a newcomer in his first year, it can't be much more than that… I think.

findings.highlight: make sure to show up twice a week
findings.evidenceJa: 週に二度、月曜と金曜に進捗報告とそこまでの成果物を提出すること
findings.explanation: The requirement is to submit progress reports and completed material twice a week, on Monday and Friday. The source does not require physical attendance, which matters because the assignment explicitly permits remote and flexible work.
findings.japanese:
「ただ、週に二度、月曜と金曜に進捗報告と
そこまでの成果物を提出すること」
findings.todokanai: "Just make sure to show up twice a week. I'll want your progress reports on Mondays and Fridays, including everything you've finished so far."

findings.highlight: They never mentioned that, did they, Hamada-san
findings.evidenceJa: 言ってませんでしたよねぇ浜田さん
findings.explanation: Haruki abruptly redirects Hamada's question by accusing Hamada himself of not having told him. The translation makes the Toumas the people who failed to mention it, weakening the deliberate conversational dodge that hides Haruki's prior contact.
findings.japanese: 「言ってませんでしたよねぇ浜田さん！」
findings.todokanai: "They never mentioned that, did they, Hamada-san!?"

findings.highlight: I've heard rumors
findings.evidenceJa: ええ、そうなんです………か
findings.explanation: Haruki almost says 'yes, that's right' from firsthand knowledge and then changes the final particle into 'is that so?' The translation invents rumors as an explicit source of knowledge and replaces the source's one-syllable near-slip.
findings.japanese: 「ええ、そうなんです………か」
findings.todokanai: "Yes, that's right… I've heard rumors."

findings.highlight: the location for her recitals
findings.evidenceJa: 練習場所も変える
findings.explanation: They will also change Kazusa's practice location. The translation turns private rehearsal space into a venue for recitals.
findings.japanese:
「今後は他社の目をくらますという意味もあって、
二人は別々に都内に部屋を借りたらしい。
ついでに練習場所も変えるそうだ」
findings.todokanai: "From now on, it appears they'll live separately in different apartments to avoid other magazines. This includes the location for her recitals."

findings.highlight: leads only in a worse direction
findings.evidenceJa: その特別が悪い方向に働くことだってある
findings.explanation: Haruki says their special history can also work in a bad direction. The translation says it leads only in a worse direction, changing a dangerous possibility into an exclusive certainty.
findings.japanese:
…ということにしないとやってられない。
だって、その特別が悪い方向に働くことだってある。
findings.todokanai: …I can't do this job without that mindset. After all, that special circumstance leads only in a worse direction.

findings.highlight: Hamada-san opens a brown envelope
findings.evidenceJa: 浜田さんから渡された茶封筒を開くと
findings.explanation: Haruki opens the brown envelope Hamada handed him. The translation makes Hamada open it, shifting the discovery action away from the focal character.
findings.japanese:
と、浜田さんから渡された茶封筒を開くと、
中から軽い金属音とともにこぼれてきたのは…
findings.todokanai: Hamada-san opens a brown envelope, and something falls out of it with a clang.

findings.highlight: responsible for all of Touma Kazusa's privileges
findings.evidenceJa: 冬馬かずさの権利を管理してる
findings.explanation: The company manages Kazusa's rights, which Haruki uses to argue that its permission makes the coverage authorized. 'Privileges' is a different legal and ethical concept and obscures the management-versus-personal-consent conflict.
findings.japanese:
「冬馬かずさの権利を管理してるのは、
株式会社冬馬曜子オフィスだよ。
…そこがいいと言えば、それはもうＯＫなんだ」
findings.todokanai: "It's Touma Youko Office PLC that's responsible for all of Touma Kazusa's privileges. …Everything will be alright so long as they give the word."

findings.highlight: set in stone since hundreds of years ago
findings.evidenceJa: そんな前提、数年前から骨身に染みてるはず
findings.explanation: Kazusa should have internalized that corporate premise over the past several years. The translation expands a few years of personal experience into hundreds of years of historical custom.
findings.japanese:
そんな前提、数年前から骨身に染みてるはずなのに、
かずさは今さら子供みたいな理屈で拗ねてみせる。
findings.todokanai: Those rules regarding contracts have been set in stone since hundreds of years ago, but Kazusa sulks like a child over it.

findings.highlight: your recitals and concerts
findings.evidenceJa: 練習とかコンサートとか
findings.explanation: Haruki expected to follow official practice sessions and concerts. Replacing practice with recitals turns the private working process into an additional public performance category.
findings.japanese:
「けどそれは練習とかコンサートとか、
一応、オフィシャルの場だけのつもりだった。
こんな、プライベートにまで侵食するなんて…」
findings.todokanai: "But I only meant it to be about your recitals and concerts. At the very least, only about official topics. I never thought it would encroach on your privacy too…"

findings.highlight: She threw out all my luggage in the freezing winter
findings.evidenceJa: トランク一つで、冬の寒空の中に放り出されて
findings.explanation: Kazusa says she herself was cast out into the winter cold with only one trunk. The translation makes the luggage the thing Youko threw out and inflates the single trunk to all of Kazusa's luggage.
findings.japanese:
「ホテルだって、チェックアウトさせられて、
トランク一つで、冬の寒空の中に放り出されて…」
findings.todokanai: "She even forced me to check out of the hotel. She threw out all my luggage in the freezing winter…"

findings.highlight: is indulgent the other
findings.evidenceJa: ワガママを言ってみたり
findings.explanation: Kazusa alternates between being considerate and making selfish demands. 'Is indulgent' normally means she indulges someone else, reversing the interpersonal direction of her demanding behavior.
findings.japanese:
気を使ってみたり、ワガママを言ってみたり、
雪菜のことを気にしてみたり、
雪菜を気にする俺を気にしてみたり。
findings.todokanai: She tries to be considerate one second, and is indulgent the other. She worries about Setsuna one second, and worries about me worrying about Setsuna the other.

findings.highlight: white noodles
findings.evidenceJa: しらたきまで
findings.explanation: The ingredient is shirataki, translucent konjac noodles with a specific hot-pot role, not generic white wheat noodles.
findings.japanese:
「あ、こら！　お前のより入ってるじゃないか！
ああっ、しらたきまでっ！」
findings.todokanai: "Ah, hey! You're putting in even more than before! Aah, you're even putting in white noodles now!"

findings.highlight: my very own creation, consisting of a random assortment of ingredients
findings.evidenceJa: 適当に食材をぶち込み“自称”寄せ鍋の完成
findings.explanation: Haruki mockingly declares the result a self-proclaimed yose-nabe after throwing ingredients together. The translation omits the named hot-pot dish and replaces it with a generic personal creation.
findings.japanese:
近くのスーパーで、急いで食材を買い込み、
テーブルと電気鍋と食器を持ち込んで、
適当に食材をぶち込み“自称”寄せ鍋の完成。
findings.todokanai: I rushed to the supermarket and bought ingredients, then brought a table, an electric cooking pot, and some tableware. Now my very own creation, consisting of a random assortment of ingredients, is done.

findings.highlight: Once someone relieves you of a certain affliction, it's easy to forget about that affliction along with any sense of gratitude
findings.evidenceJa: 喉元過ぎればというか、衣食足りてなお文句を言うというか
findings.explanation: Haruki juxtaposes one shortened proverb with a comic reversal of another: once the heat passes one forgets it, and even with food and clothing satisfied she still complains. The translation expands only the first idea and drops the second punch line.
findings.japanese:
…喉元過ぎればというか、
衣食足りてなお文句を言うというか。
findings.todokanai: …Once someone relieves you of a certain affliction, it's easy to forget about that affliction along with any sense of gratitude.

findings.highlight: I brought with me some noodles
findings.evidenceJa: 引っ越し蕎麦がある
findings.explanation: The item is explicitly hikkoshi soba, invoking the Japanese moving custom and Youko's earlier joke about greeting neighbors. The translation reduces it to unspecified noodles Haruki happened to bring.
findings.japanese:
「そういえば、引っ越し蕎麦があるんだけど、
鍋に入れれば良かったかな？」
findings.todokanai: "By the way, I brought with me some noodles. Should I have put it in the pot?"

findings.highlight: going on the front page
findings.evidenceJa: 表紙用の撮影
findings.explanation: The earlier professional shoot was for a magazine cover, not a newspaper-like front page.
findings.japanese:
「あれは表紙用の撮影だからな。
それだって昔はスタジオ借りてやってたんだぞ」
findings.todokanai: "That was because the pictures were going on the front page. Even those used to be done in rented studios."

findings.highlight: I'm the only employee in an independent studio
findings.evidenceJa: まるで同人誌作りの勢いだ
findings.explanation: Haruki likens handling interviews, photography, writing, and editing himself to making a doujinshi. The translation invents a one-employee independent studio and loses the self-publishing comparison.
findings.japanese:
もともと最近の雑誌編集の仕事の範囲は広いけど、
今度はインタビューから写真撮影、記事の執筆、
編集までって、まるで同人誌作りの勢いだ。
findings.todokanai: The job of a magazine editor has always been broad, but this time it's interviewing, taking pictures, writing articles, and even editing. It's almost like I'm the only employee in an independent studio.

findings.highlight: Shandy Editing of The Orient Magazine
findings.evidenceJa: 東邦出版のシャンディ
findings.explanation: Shandy is one of the major women's fashion magazines published by Touhou Publishing. The translation again invents an 'Orient Magazine' and makes Shandy Editing a subordinate unit.
findings.japanese:
「東邦出版のシャンディって名乗ったんだろ？
それ、三大女性ファッション誌の一つだぞ？
表紙に載ると電車の中吊りにまでお前が出てくる」
findings.todokanai: "She said she was part of Shandy Editing of The Orient Magazine, right? That's one of the big three women's fashion magazines. If you're on their front page, you'll definitely end up on advertising posters on trains."

findings.highlight: As long as my output meets their expectations
findings.evidenceJa: アウトプットさえ期限通りに出せれば
findings.explanation: Haruki's freedom is conditional on delivering output on time. The translation replaces the explicit deadline with an undefined quality expectation.
findings.japanese: …アウトプットさえ期限通りに出せればだけど。
findings.todokanai: …As long as my output meets their expectations.
